heading: Scintillator and SiPM
content: A 5 × 5 × 1 cm slab of plastic scintillator as the detection medium, giving about 10,000 photons per MeV. A 6 × 6 mm SiPM for light collection: single-photon sensitive, nanosecond response, and not affected by magnetic fields.

heading: Fast, low-noise electronics
content: A custom PCB shapes the signal, and the Raspberry Pi Pico measures it with a 12-bit ADC. One core takes data while the other runs the screen and card, so dead time is about 400 µs per event and it logs up to 700 events per second.

heading: Sensors on every event
content: Temperature, barometric pressure, acceleration and angular velocity are recorded with each event, so you can look for correlations with the weather or track how the detector moved.

heading: Take it anywhere
content: It draws 0.5 W from any USB port and weighs 110 g in its aluminum case; a 5,000 mAh power bank runs two detectors for 18 hours. Detectors have flown on high-altitude balloons, sounding rockets and the International Space Station.
